logic.note: TRIG pulses shorter than 10 µs are ignored, a new trigger is ignored while a measurement runs, ECHO is a push-pull 5 V output.

timing.note: Cycle-exact on the MCU clock: ECHO rises 460 µs after TRIG falls (200 µs 40 kHz burst + module processing) and stays HIGH distance × 2 / speed-of-sound (58.2 µs/cm at 20 °C), or 38 ms with nothing in 2–400 cm. The MCU is stopped at the exact cycle so pulseIn() measures it correctly.

analog.note: The target is a single distance: a prop, or from the physics world the nearest hit of 7 rays over ±15° (a 30° cone, roughly what measured beam patterns show for walls and large objects; the datasheet's 15° 'effectual angle' is for small targets). No beam pattern, no soft or angled surfaces that absorb or deflect the sound, no multipath, no noise.

power.note: Constant 15 mA load on VCC; it measures only with VCC ≥ 4.5 V.

radio.note: Not a radio part (ultrasound is not modelled as a medium).

emulates: Echo pulse width proportional to distance
doesNotEmulate: Beam shape and side lobes (here 7 rays over ±15°; a thin pole at the edge of that cone may not echo on hardware)
Soft, round or angled targets that return no echo
Measurement noise (± 0.3–1 cm) and occasional zero readings
Minimum time between pings (~60 ms recommended)
testOnRealDevice: Readings on soft (fabric), round or angled obstacles
Two sensors pinging at the same time
Ping rate faster than every 60 ms
